problem: The attenuation formula Vout = Vin × R₂/(R₁+R₂) is dropped into the amplification formula set before attenuation is introduced in the text, and it never says the output is taken across R₂. A student can misread it as part of the amplifier gain.
fix: Move the divider formula to the attenuation paragraph, and write: Vout = Vin × R₂/(R₁+R₂), where R₁ is the series resistor from the input and R₂ is the resistor to ground across which Vout is measured.

problem: "That removes 50 Hz hum" overstates what a 15.9 Hz first-order filter does; the same section later shows the hum is only cut to 0.303 of its value (about -10.4 dB).
fix: "That cuts 50 Hz hum to about 30 % of its value but also slows a fast strain pulse."

problem: The chain is 2 mV × gain 500 = 1.0 V, then filter, lineariser and isolator, yet the output node is labelled 0-5 V. No block in the drawn chain supplies the extra gain of about 5, so the numbers do not close.
fix: Either relabel the output node as "Output 1.0 V at full load" or add an output scaling/level stage before the 0-5 V output node.

problem: "Attenuation and impedance matching also belong here" contradicts Section 1, which already covered both; the reader is left unsure which section owns them.
fix: "Attenuation and impedance matching, covered in Section 1, also appear at this stage of a practical channel: a 0-10 V transmitter feeding a 3.3 V ADC needs a divider."
